abstract.t:
This document defines the Lightspeed Notification Protocol (LSN), a hardware-accelerated signaling mechanism designed for sub-100 microsecond network convergence in AI/ML data center fabrics. By remaining on chip and never punting to the host CPU, LSN bypasses traditional CPU-based latencies to propagate link failures and congestion via a hardware-efficient encoding. It serves as a high- speed complement to routing protocols such as BGP, providing an immediate hardware veto that prunes failed or congested paths while maintaining control-plane stability for path recovery.
The same mechanism applies inside the DC Clos and, in some deployments, across the Data Center Interconnect (DCI) and WAN. This document defines two encoding modes: a dense encoding for DC fabrics, where traffic is load-balanced over many ECMP spines, and a sparse encoding for the DCI and WAN.
